content.text: Section 22 fully matches the preferred position, and no competing audit/monitoring rights exist elsewhere.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 already meets the preferred position in full: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period, require thirty days' prior written notice, occur during normal business hours without unreasonable disruption, are conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and are at Vendor's cost unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent (§ 22.2). Section 22.2 also expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or third-party confidential information, satisfying the no-direct-system-access requirement. Section 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are Customer Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of final report, shortfall payment resolves the issue). No other audit, inspection, verification, or remote monitoring right binding Customer appears elsewhere in the Agreement, so no redline is needed.
